limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local efficacy validation.
Original typed source inventory is not normalized; retain source identities and limits in the procedure/readsets.

applicability.scope: Pinned vLLM V1 branch-based diagnosis of queued requests, low scheduled-token counts and KV-pressure preemption, separating admission/token/input/allocation/connector-wait constraints.
applicability.prerequisites: The deployed scheduler must be mapped to the pinned branches, with effective configuration and a bounded request/step trace; another revision requires re-establishing that correspondence.
applicability.input_contract: Deployed revision, scheduler class/configuration, connector role, KV layout, policy and speculative/encoder/concurrent-batch features; per-step queues, tokens, both budgets, allocation results, victims, transfer/free state and timing.
applicability.produced_artifact: A per-step accounting ledger, observed limiting branch and competing explanation, missing instrumentation and one conditional configuration/progress hypothesis with predicted effects and trade-offs.
applicability.failure_modes: Inferring memory exhaustion from a queue or high KV usage, conflating token/input budgets, ignoring pending frees or reading async token accounting as load completion can attribute admission stalls to the wrong branch.
applicability.refusal_point: When required state is missing, leave the diagnosis unresolved and request the smallest trace; escalate allocation or connector behavior outside the readset and stop before live mutation or performance claims.

recommendations: Trace the first actual blocking or skip branch and record running versus admission caps and token versus input budgets separately.
Inspect deferred frees and request-free eligibility before blaming preemption victim selection, then reconcile restored budgets for an already-scheduled victim.
Reconstruct waiting admission independently, including queue precedence and async prefix states; change no setting without a branch-specific hypothesis.
